text.p: Anglo-Australian miner RTZ-CRA said on Wednesday inventories of copper concentrates and intermediate products containing about 60,000 tonnes of copper were on hand as of December 31 at its Kennecott Utah subsidiary.
"Most of this copper is already contracted for sale and will be delivered to customers and priced during 1997," the company said in its fourth quarter and calendar 1996 production report.
The company also said it had provisionally priced 253 million pounds of copper at an average US$0.98 a pound.
RTZ-CRA said the Kennecott flash smelting furnace was now performing near design.
But output from the flash converting furnace remained below expectations, due in large part to bottlenecks in the anode refining and casting facilities, the report said.
RTZ-CRA has said the flash converting furnace would be shut down for about six weeks in the first half of 1997 to replace the refractory and install new cooling blocks.
"Improvements will be made in anode refining and casting at the same time, subject to availability of necessary components, the report said.
The flash smelting furnace and acid plant would be down for maintenance for about 10 days during this period, but would otherwise continue to operate to produce matte, RTZ-CRA said.
